<!-- pr-reviewer: 075921bfa65c0d20c93f177daf863872468bc011 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- No pick = the old route: `contour_start::seat` with `picked == None` runs the same three steps in the same order as before (axis reseat, control mid-run seam, lead-room reseat). The pick is `Option`, absent means unchanged. No existing golden is touched (only the new `contour_start_point.cl`).
- Re-sequencing (`start_at`) rotates the same closed vertex list and inserts the foot of the pick: direction, compensation side and every level are kept. Only the picked ring is re-seated (`pi == li` on the same area-sorted `loops`); other rings keep the automatic seam.
- The lead is planned by the existing `seam_leads` / `extend_leads` at the new start, then `lead_held` refuses by name if a lead-in was asked for and the lead law left none. A pick is never moved and never cuts without the asked-for lead.
- Refusals are by name: too-far pick (1.5 D + stock), tabs, control/wear comp, open chain, tilted contour, other op kinds. Validation at command creation (finite, within 1 km). Project field is `skip_serializing_if` + `serde(default)`, so old files load unchanged. Digest grows only when set. No unwrap/expect/panic. New domain code is in motion, app only wires params/project. Provenance line present; `contour_start.rs` is 179 lines. Decision record included.

**Results merged with main (7cd6e655a), on the self-hosted runner: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/43481169191**
- Quick gate: motion suites ok (148 s), app suites ok (866 s), ui suites ok (118 s), 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: run green.
- Not run: a new test against main's code (the tests need the new field, so they cannot compile there).

**Requested before merge**
- None blocking. On the unpinned "no lead-in fits at the pick" refusal: not a blocker, because it only refuses (the failure direction is safe) and the guard is a four-line check. But it is the one place where a wrong pick could otherwise plunge without a lead, so please pin it in #1473 or sooner (a narrow-room fixture with a long linear lead).

**Notes**
- The pick is never checked to lie on the wall side that is cut, only within reach; the lead law is the guard. Fine for this slice.
- No UI row yet, so no screenshots owed.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
